investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Section 136 of the Sexual Offences At 2003 was Inserted, in relation to England, Wales and Northern Ireland, by section 21(1) of and paragraph 1 of Schedule 2 to the Policing and Crime Act 2009.
(ii) See section 136C(3) and (4) and section 136F(2) and (4) of the Sexual offences Act 2003 for the prescribed actions.
(iii) Section 22 of the Policing and Crime Act 2009 disables section 127 of the Magistrates' Courts Act 1980 by creating a new section 132A in the Sexual Offences Act 2003. It also provides for the offence to be charged even if committed before the commencement of the section.

other.penalty:
Summary: Fifty one weeks imprisonment OR a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Note:
Until the commencement of section 281(5) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 the reference to 51 weeks is to be read as a reference to 6 months.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
